summary: Iteration 101: Business Tool Access System (3-tier: none/standard/advanced) testing complete. All 23 backend pytest tests passed. Backend APIs for admin user detail, setting access level, my-permissions, access-level endpoint, and panel access control are working correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: ✓ PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/business-tool-access sets access level to 'none', 'standard', or 'advanced'
✓ PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/business-tool-access returns 400 for invalid user ID
✓ GET /api/business-tools/access-level returns correct level and limits (maxPanels: 10, maxFieldsPerPanel: 20)
✓ Platform admin can list panels (bypasses access check via is_platform_admin)
✓ Platform admin can create panels (bypasses access check via is_platform_admin)
✓ Access level changes persist correctly in database
✓ All endpoints require authentication (return 401/403/422 without auth header)
seed_data_creation: Test panels created with TEST_ prefix are cleaned up after tests
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 101 tested the Business Tool Access System (3-tier: none/standard/advanced). All backend APIs work correctly with dev-test-token authentication. Key findings: (1) businessToolAccess field is included in admin user detail and my-permissions responses, (2) Admin can set access level via PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/business-tool-access, (3) Invalid values are rejected with 400, (4) Platform admins always get 'advanced' access regardless of stored field (is_platform_admin check bypasses access level). Note: To test standard access blocking for panel CRUD, you would need a non-admin user since platform admins bypass the access check.
features_tested: Platform admin bypasses access check for panel CRUD
Access level changes persist in database
notes: The dev-test-token user is a platform admin (isAdmin=true), so require_advanced_access() always passes for them via is_platform_admin check. This is correct behavior - platform admins always have advanced access regardless of the stored businessToolAccess field. To properly test access restriction for standard users, a non-admin test user would be needed.
